_This page is generated from src/capabilities.ts and src/harnesses/, so it says what the tool does._

Coding agents do not report the same things. One shows which agent made each tool call, and another shows only the final answer. Each harness adapter declares the `capabilities` it can deliver. A case, or a check in it, can need some. A case that needs something the harness lacks is **not applicable** on that harness.

A not-applicable case has no runs and no score. The report lists it with the capabilities that are missing. It is never a pass and never a failure, because a check that cannot see what it looks for would pass or fail for the wrong reason.

## What a case needs

A case needs what its `requires` key lists, and what its checks need. A check needs what its own `requires` key lists, and what its type implies. A harness that lacks any of them cannot run the case.

```json
{
  "requires": ["mcp", "bin:git"],
  "checks": [{ "type": "output_contains", "text": "done" }]
}
```

A capability that begins with `bin:` is a host capability: an executable of that name on `PATH`. It is met on every harness when the executable is there, and on none when it is not. `check` prints the ones that the loaded cases ask for.

## Skip one check

By default one check that needs something missing makes the whole case not applicable. A check with `"ifUnsupported": "skip"` is dropped instead. The weights of the other checks are re-normalized, and the report lists the case under "Ran with checks skipped" with the skipped checks named. A case whose every check would be skipped is not applicable.

```json
{
  "checks": [
    { "type": "output_contains", "text": "done" },
    {
      "type": "tool_called",
      "kind": "subagent",
      "requires": ["childCalls"],
      "ifUnsupported": "skip"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Name the harnesses

A `harnesses` list on a case limits it to those harness ids. It is a last resort, because the harness may gain the capability later. It needs a `note` that says why, and the report shows the note as the reason elsewhere.

## Scores across harnesses

Each harness's suite score is over its own applicable cases, and it is printed as `score (n of N cases)`. A harness with no applicable case gets a line in the report and no score. When more than one harness runs, the report adds a common-set score over the cases that apply to all of them. Only that number compares harnesses. If no case applies to any harness that ran, the command stops with exit code 2.

## The capabilities

| Capability      | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `subagents`     | The stream shows when the agent starts another agent, as a tool call of the kind `subagent`.                                                                                             |
| `multiTurn`     | The harness takes more than one prompt in one session, so a case can have several turns.                                                                                                 |
| `userInvoke`    | A case can invoke a skill the way a user does, with a slash command, and not through the agent's own tool call.                                                                          |
| `toolOutputs`   | The stream carries what each tool returned, so a check can read a tool's output.                                                                                                         |
| `assistantText` | The stream carries the agent's text between its tool calls, not only its final answer.                                                                                                   |
| `turnGrouping`  | The stream says which tool calls belong to one assistant turn, so a check can ask for calls in the same turn.                                                                            |
| `childCalls`    | The stream attributes each tool call to the agent that made it, so a check can tell a subagent's calls from the parent's.                                                                |
| `childText`     | The stream carries the text that a subagent wrote, apart from the parent's.                                                                                                              |
| `rules`         | The adapter installs the subject's rules and instruction file (the config's `rules` and `instructionFile`) the way the harness reads them, so a case can plant a rule and see it obeyed. |
| `rulesReport`   | The harness reports the rule and instruction texts it loaded, so a check can show that a rule reached the model.                                                                         |
| `hooks`         | The stream shows each hook that ran, with its event, exit code and the context it added, so a check can read a hook's result.                                                            |
| `history`       | A case can start from a conversation that already happened, written into the first prompt or into the harness's own store.                                                               |
| `historyNative` | A case can start from a conversation written into the harness's own session store and resumed from it.                                                                                   |
| `askUser`       | The stream shows when the agent asks the user a question, so a case can answer it.                                                                                                       |
| `toolDurations` | The stream says how long each tool call took, so a check can bound it.                                                                                                                   |
| `sessionStore`  | The harness keeps its sessions in files that a run can read after it ends.                                                                                                               |
| `compact`       | A case can compact the conversation between turns.                                                                                                                                       |
| `clear`         | A case can clear the conversation between turns.                                                                                                                                         |
| `resume`        | A case can resume an earlier session in a later run.                                                                                                                                     |
| `mcp`           | The harness starts the MCP servers that a case configures, and the stream shows their tool calls.                                                                                        |
| `skillListing`  | The harness lists the skills it loaded at startup, so a run whose subject is missing from the list is invalid.                                                                           |
| `loadedReport`  | The harness reports the plugins and skills it loaded at startup, which `--isolated` and the subject-loaded test read.                                                                    |
| `isolated`      | The harness starts with nothing loaded but what the run gives it and proves that from its report, so `--isolated` can promise it. It needs `loadedReport` too.                           |
| `sandbox`       | The harness can run its tools in a sandbox that denies the network and the files outside the workspace.                                                                                  |

## What each harness declares

An adapter declares a capability only when a parser test proves it on a stream. `yes` means that it does. A cell that says `no` is not a claim that the harness cannot do it, only that no test proves it yet.

| Capability      | `pi` | `claude-code` | `cursor` | `opencode` | `codex` |
| --------------- | ---- | ------------- | -------- | ---------- | ------- |
| `subagents`     | no   | yes           | yes      | yes        | yes     |
| `multiTurn`     | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `userInvoke`    | no   | no            | no       | no         | no      |
| `toolOutputs`   | yes  | yes           | no       | yes        | yes     |
| `assistantText` | yes  | yes           | no       | yes        | yes     |
| `turnGrouping`  | yes  | yes           | no       | yes        | no      |
| `childCalls`    | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `childText`     | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `rules`         | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `rulesReport`   | no   | no            | no       | no         | no      |
| `hooks`         | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `history`       | yes  | yes           | yes      | yes        | yes     |
| `historyNative` | no   | no            | no       | no         | no      |
| `askUser`       | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `toolDurations` | no   | no            | no       | yes        | no      |
| `sessionStore`  | no   | no            | no       | no         | no      |
| `compact`       | no   | no            | no       | no         | no      |
| `clear`         | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `resume`        | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `mcp`           | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `skillListing`  | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `loadedReport`  | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `isolated`      | no   | yes           | no       | no         | no      |
| `sandbox`       | no   | no            | no       | no         | no      |

| Harness       | Status       | What the status says                                                                       |
| ------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pi`          | `scripted`   | The real CLI ran through the adapter against a scripted model endpoint. No real model ran. |
| `claude-code` | `real-model` | A real model ran through the adapter, so its stream is a capture.                          |
| `cursor`      | `unverified` | The adapter was written from the CLI's documentation. No run confirmed it.                 |
| `opencode`    | `scripted`   | The real CLI ran through the adapter against a scripted model endpoint. No real model ran. |
| `codex`       | `scripted`   | The real CLI ran through the adapter against a scripted model endpoint. No real model ran. |

[What was verified](../agents/verified.md) says how each adapter was proven. [Write a case](../guides/write-a-case.md) shows the keys.
